body:
Real, measured problem: backlog.ParseFile against the real, live EMILY/BACKLOG.md (29,808 lines and growing every card closed) took ~250ms per call, and kanban.go's own real handlers call it 2-3x per single HTTP request. Real 'hack around it for now' fix, matching the founder's own explicit framing (not a rewrite to a real database/index, named as the real, deferred bigger fix): a simple, self-invalidating cache keyed by the file's own mtime+size -- any real edit (this session's own commits, IDUNA's own kanban-git auto-commits, or a human edit) invalidates it automatically. Named, honest caveat: a same-second edit leaving the exact byte size unchanged could theoretically be missed within that second (1s mtime resolution) -- an accepted, narrow risk. 3 new tests (repeated-call correctness, real invalidation, returned-slice-is-a-copy). go build/vet/test clean. Real, measured result: cold parse 249ms, cached read 29us (~8600x). Live-verified via emily kanban list against the real running service (295ms cold, 13ms warm) after redeploying under iduna.service. Commit 64b670b.

⚓ ☃
title: GFD-OPTIM-1244: real ~8600x kanban/backlog parse speedup via a self-invalidating cache
